claims.text: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy has been associated with a two-fold increased risk for transient global amnesia.
claims.evidence: TTC has been associated with a two-fold increased risk for TGA

claims.text: In Takotsubo cardiomyopathy, the pathophysiological mechanism likely resides in a catecholamine storm triggered by emotional or physical stress with consequent activation of hypothalamo-pituitary-adrenal and sympatho-adrenomedullary axis.
claims.evidence: the pathophysiological mechanism resides probably in a catecholamine storm, triggered...by emotional or physical stress with consequent activation of hypotalamo-pituitary-adrenal and sympatho-adrenomedullary axis in TTC

claims.text: Sympathetic nerve fiber density and beta receptors for circulating adrenaline show an inverse pattern in the myocardium, which could explain the preferential involvement of apical myocardium in Takotsubo cardiomyopathy.
claims.evidence: Sympathetic nerve fiber density and beta receptors for circulating adrenaline show an inverse pattern...This observation could explain the preferential involvement...of the apical myocardium in TTC

claims.text: A single, common pathological pathway between Takotsubo cardiomyopathy and transient global amnesia is not self-evident, with uncertainty about whether there is a common cause or if one condition elicits the other.
claims.evidence: a single, common pathological pathway between TTC and TGA is not self-evident. In particular, it is unclear whether there is a common cause...or if one condition...could elicit the other

claims.text: Low cortisol blood levels in patients with chronic stress may represent a compensatory mechanism to avoid hypercortisolism, leaving the adrenaline effect on the heart unbalanced.
claims.evidence: low cortisol blood levels have been reported in patients with chronic stress as a compensatory mechanism to avoid hypercortisolism...thus leaving the adrenaline effect...unbalanced

claims.text: Beta-blockers may improve long-term cardiac outcome in patients with Takotsubo syndrome but do not show a secondary preventive effect on syndrome recurrence.
claims.evidence: The same study showed absence of a secondary preventive effect on TTS recurrence even though BBs may improve the long-term cardiac outcome in patients with TTS

claims.text: There is limited retrospective evidence that beta-blockers could have a benefit on 1-year survival of patients with cardiogenic shock due to Takotsubo syndrome.
claims.evidence: there is...limited retrospective evidence that the BB could have a benefit on the 1-year survival of patients with cardiogenic shock because of TTS

claims.text: Early recognition of concomitant Takotsubo cardiomyopathy in asymptomatic patients with primary neurological conditions is clinically important.
claims.evidence: Awareness for the possibility of a concomitant cardiac pathology in asymptomatic patients with primary neurological conditions seems to be important
